subject: Request: Audit of SLA credit calculation and evidence — Palisade Systems
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@palisade.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: 2026-11-18 latency incident — request for SLA credit and timeline

Hi Irene,

We observed sustained latency spikes against our production inference endpoints on 2026-11-18 between approximately 02:50 UTC and 05:10 UTC. Impact: our inference p95 latency increased from ~120ms to ~1.4s for the affected window, causing downstream queuing and a visible degradation in our product. We captured traces and request ids, and have attached a short CSV with the timeline.

Palisade is on a committed Dedicated plan (monthly committed spend $45,000). Per the SLA language, this looks like it may be eligible for a service credit. Could you confirm:
- Whether Redwood classifies this window as eligible downtime for an SLA credit?
- How you calculate the credit (formula and inputs you use)?
- Expected timing to issue any approved credit and the format (invoice adjustment vs. standalone credit)?

Attached: palisade-sla-timeline.csv (timeline and sample request IDs).

Thanks — we need a response for our internal billing review by EOD Monday.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Reliability, Palisade Systems
liam.oconnor@palisade.com
[Attachment: palisade-sla-timeline.csv (text/csv)]

Subject: Re: 2026-11-18 latency incident — request for SLA credit and timeline

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 11:02 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus: can you confirm the affected time window and volume-adjusted uptime for 2026-11-18?

Attached are the raw sample logs and a short extraction I ran against our metrics store. Quick summary:
- Observed degradation window: 2026-11-18T02:49:30Z to 2026-11-18T05:07:15Z (approx 2h17m).
- Population affected: 4 of 12 dedicated instances serving Palisade's pool; p95 latency increased to ~1.3–1.6s during peak.
- Root cause: kernel scheduling anomaly on a subset of hosts after a late-night kernel update push (rollout of 5.18.7 -> 5.18.8). We rolled back the update at 04:58Z which restored baseline latency.
- SLA exclusions: no customer-configured overrides or misconfig on Palisade's side; the event is on our infra side and not an excluded maintenance window.

I've uploaded the full log bundle to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz-palisade-sla-audit (see palisade-raw-logs-20261118.zip).

[Attachment: palisade-raw-logs-20261118.zip (application/zip)]

Marcus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: 2026-11-18 latency incident — request for SLA credit and timeline

Hi team — I ran the eligibility through our credit calculator (policy v3.2). Methodology we used:
- Determine affected minutes within customer's allocated service window and convert to percentage of monthly service availability (minutes_affected / total_minutes_in_billing_period).
- Multiply that percentage by 1x monthly committed spend for first-tier incidents (per SLA table) to determine gross credit amount.
- Apply prorate adjustments for multi-zone redundancy (Palisade has cross-AZ redundancy configured; we applied a 0.85 factor).

Inputs and result (rounded):
- Billing period total minutes: 43,200 (30-day month)
- Minutes affected: 137 (2h17m -> 137 minutes)
- Impact percentage: 0.317%
- Monthly committed spend: $45,000
- Gross credit (1x): $142.65 (0.00317 * 45,000)
- Redundancy factor (0.85) -> net credit: $121.25 -> rounded to $121.25

Recommendation: issue a $121.25 service credit applied to Palisade's next invoice. We should include a short reconciliation sheet that shows the window, logs link, and the calculation.

Attachments: credit-approval-sheet.xlsx (includes steps and cell formulas).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
AM, Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: 2026-11-18 latency incident — request for SLA credit and timeline

Hi Liam — thanks again for flagging this and for the sample timeline. We completed our internal audit and have approved a service credit. Summary for Palisade Systems:

What happened
- On 2026-11-18 we observed a kernel scheduling anomaly on a subset of hosts that temporarily increased p95 latency for a portion of Palisade's dedicated pool. The team rolled back the kernel update at 04:58 UTC which restored baseline performance. Full logs and traces are available here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz-palisade-sla-audit (see palisade-raw-logs-20261118.zip).

Credit calculation
- Affected minutes: 137 (2026-11-18T02:49:30Z -> 2026-11-18T05:07:15Z).
- Calculation: (minutes_affected / minutes_in_billing_period) * monthly_commitment * SLA_factor (1x) * redundancy_prorate (0.85)
- Resulting credit: $121.25 (credit memo will be applied to your next invoice). We attached a short reconciliation with the cell-level math.

Next steps
- Finance will create a credit memo referencing DL-20231009-PAL and apply it within 7–10 business days.
- If Palisade prefers a standalone refund instead of an invoice credit, please let us know and we will route to billing ops.
- I'll follow up with a postmortem summary for your SRE team by end-of-week that outlines the corrective actions we took (patch gating + improved rollout checks).

Attachments: credit-approval-sheet.xlsx; palisade-sla-timeline.csv
DocuSign link for official acknowledgement (optional): https://docusign.com/requests/3f4a9c

Please let me know if you need any additional detail for your internal billing audit.

Best,
Irene Choi
